rationale: No displayed candidate contains the distinctive arms-and-munitions classification, the category sequence, or the statutory machinery for proclaiming a periodically revised list under section 12(i) of the 1939 joint resolution. C18 and C05 are the strongest formal analogues because they are proclamations that invoke statutory authority and prescribe detailed product lists, but their tariff schedules and trade-agreement machinery are materially different. C07 shares only standard proclamation form and a described-property list. These similarities are generic or structural at too broad a level to establish a reusable drafting template.

shared_material.child_excerpt: acting under and by virtue of the authority conferred upon me by the said joint resolution ... hereby declare and proclaim that the articles listed below shall ... be considered arms, ammunition, and implements of war
shared_material.parent_excerpt: acting under the authority of said section 350 of the Tariff Act of 1930, as amended, do hereby proclaim ... such modifications of existing duties and other import restrictions
shared_material.explanation: C18 shares a statutory-authority proclamation followed by operative treatment of listed products, but this is general proclamation architecture and distinct tariff machinery rather than concrete language or provisions adapted into the child.

shared_material.parent_excerpt: the rates of duty and import tax specified in the column at the right of the respective descriptions of products listed ... shall be applied
shared_material.explanation: C05 likewise uses detailed product enumeration, but the list administers tariff rates and amendments rather than defining a regulated class of military articles.
